memo_h: a high score is not proof
memo_s1p: The detector gives a probability, not conclusive proof. It can be wrong: in 0–2% of cases it may mistake an ordinary human text for AI work (on student essays — even more often). Never lower a grade or punish a person based only on the percentage shown by the program.
memo_s2p: Ask how the text was written: drafts, notes, sources. A person may have polished their writing with AI, and an AI text may have been edited by hand — the score can't tell these cases apart.
memo_s3p: Compare with the author's earlier work; look for sudden jumps in style, facts the author couldn't know, or references that don't exist. Re-check the text in Precise mode.
memo_s4p: Save the report (CSV/printout) with the date and mode, and write down what you decided and why. When in doubt, show the text to a second reader.
memo_sub: For teachers and editors: what to do when the detector shows a high percentage.

qa4_a: English is the main language, but Russian and Polish now run on the same models. On our held-out test sets (350 AI and 350 human texts per language) the verdict “AI” catches about 80% (Polish) and 78% (Russian) of AI texts at 0.9% and 0.6% false alarms (version 1.1: 39% and 57%). Texts from newer models and rewritten texts are caught less often (Gemini-rewritten Polish: 48%, Russian: 50%). The sets are small, expect ±5 points. We have not measured Russian or Polish against other detectors, so we make no comparison claim. Other languages are not supported. Exact figures are in the results section.

res_chi_th: Chicago Booth test, strict setting (1% false alarms)
res_grp_hu: Human-written texts — wrongly flagged, % (lower is better)
res_lang_h: Russian and Polish: what changed in 1.3.1
res_lang_p: Russian and Polish now run on the same models as English. On our held-out test sets (350 AI + 350 human texts per language) the verdict “AI” catches about 79% (Polish) and 80% (Russian) of AI texts at 1.4% and 0.6% false alarms (version 1.1: 39% and 57%; Polish false alarms were 0.9% in 1.3). Texts rewritten by another model are caught less often (Gemini-rewritten: Polish 56%, Russian 59%). The sets are small, so expect ±5 points. We did not compare Russian or Polish against other detectors.
res_r1: HumanizerBench: 16 rewriting tools, 1,675 texts (kept only for testing, never used in training)
res_r2: AI Humanizer Benchmark, Oct 2026: 363 texts (separate check set, not used in training)
res_r6: MAGE: short texts, old small models
res_spd_note: CPU: 6 threads. Model loading at start takes 5–10 s. The GPU runs the models in half precision, so scores differ slightly from the CPU (about 0.1 on a scale where the AI line is near 0); verdicts matched on our checks. Measured on version 1.3; 1.3.1 has the same architecture.
res_spd_sub: The whole check on one text in the Windows app. Test computer: Ryzen 7 7800X3D processor, Radeon RX 9070 XT graphics. Older laptops are slower.
res_sub: Share of texts flagged as AI. For AI-written texts higher is better (more caught); for human texts lower is better (fewer false alarms). Measured in Sensitive mode — the “AI / not AI” line is drawn so that about 1% of ordinary human texts are flagged (on our test sets 0.2–2.0%, higher on non-native writing). Exact figures are in the tables below.
res_vs_note: Competitor verdicts as published by the benchmark operators; their thresholds are unknown, so false-positive rates are not comparable.

qa13_q: What does the percentage in the result mean?
qa13_a: It is the confidence in the verdict shown next to it (“AI”, “human” or “uncertain”), not the share of the text written by AI: 88% next to “AI” means the models are fairly sure the text is machine-written. The share of the text that looks AI-written is shown separately (the colour map, “AI share” and the authorship bar). A high percentage is a reason to look closer, not proof; see “If the score is high”. Very short texts (under about 150 words) give less reliable results, and the app warns about it.

nums2_p: the same texts after the StealthGPT rewriting tool. Pangram reaches 98%: on humanized text we are behind it.
nums3_p: caught on our own test sets, at 0.6% (Russian) and 1.4% (Polish) false alarms. The sets are small: expect ±5 points.
nums4_p: TOEFL exam essays by non-native writers are the weak spot (about 0.2–0.4% on ordinary and school texts). Use Precise mode for such work.
